claim.text: The complete four-file public-domain SWI-Prolog demo corpus at a pinned upstream commit shows Gen25 Rust accepts exactly likes.pl directly, where Gen24 accepted none; three other files remain syntax rejected, while SWI 9.0.4 exits zero with ERROR diagnostics on these, so exit 0 is not clean load.
claim.scope: Four original public-domain demo/*.pl programs at upstream commit 111385b9, native Rust Gen24 vs Gen25 ELF64 and system SWI-Prolog 9.0.4; 12 live SWI semantic likes.pl queries, 264 historical Rust CLI comparisons.
assumptions: Original public-domain source Git blobs and byte lengths match pinned repository content
One Rust true/0 load probe is a parser/loader observation, not an exhaustive semantic oracle
SWI stderr may contain ERROR despite process exit 0
SWI 9.0.4 may be older than upstream source syntax
forbidden_promotions: Do not count directory acceptance as general ISO Prolog compliance
Do not count SWI exit-zero with ERROR as successful source load
Do not treat intentionally non-executable colours.pl as an ordinary conformance failure
Do not infer runtime performance or a single-token full parser remedy
Do not call project-authored source selection independent experimental authorship

specification.intended_object: Source identity, typed Rust and SWI loader outcome, and specific independent likes semantic oracle for exactly four original third-party public-domain programs.
invariants: All four exact original Git source files and README are present and hash-verified
No source preprocessing, transformation or silent exclusions
Original Rust Gen24 and Gen25 use identical true./fixed limits probes
SWI source loader exit, stdout and stderr observed separately
Twelve independent SWI Prolog ordered likes.pl outputs match untouched Gen25
264 historical full-output Rust CLI cases preserved
known_answer_cases: likes.pl original accepted in Gen25 and syntax-rejected in Gen24
colours.pl original explicitly comments that this code does not run
all four source Git blobs and byte sizes
SWI raw exit zero with ERROR stderr is not a clean load

implementation.environment: Ubuntu 24.04 ELF64, Rust 1.85.1, SWI-Prolog 9.0.4 (source reference different release window), Python 3 stdlib
implementation.live_entrypoint: gprolog-rs original.pl true. --max-solutions 1 --max-steps 100000; swipl -q -f none -s original.pl -g true -t halt; separate 12 original likes.pl SWI reference
implementation.representation: Source SHA/byte provenance, structured triple (process exit, stdout, stderr) and explicit diagnostic/error statuses by engine

controls.compute_parity: Rust Gen24 and Gen25 compiled under the same pinned compiler+ABI; SWI is independent third-party evaluator without time/cycle comparison.
controls.parameter_parity: Identical original source files, true. query and Rust limits max_solutions 1 and max_steps 100000; 12 likes semantic control uses fixed 32 and 100000.
controls.sampling_parity: One complete same-upstream-directory four-file census, no randomized sample and no inferential population confidence.
controls.data_access_parity: Four exact source Git SHA1 and README license authority, no source preprocessing; SWI and both Rust load actual same files.

preregistration.prediction: Gen25 adds acceptance of original likes.pl relative to Gen24; other programs likely remain constrained by syntax not yet implemented; no predeclared exact error offsets for those other files.
preregistration.primary_metric: Typed complete four-source outcomes under Gen24, Gen25 and independently executed SWI; source identity, twelve likes semantic matches and 264 strict historical matches.
preregistration.uncertainty_method: Full directory descriptive enumeration, no confidence interval or general Prolog population; SWI version older than pinned 2026 source and diagnostic semantics are method-specific.
preregistration.kill_condition: Mismatched original SHA/licensing, corpus exclusion, missing SWI version, hidden preprocessing, misleading source classification, failed likes SWI answer vector or 264 strict regression.
preregistration.stop_condition: No new syntax/engine fixes or denominator edits to rescue a negative result; next feature needs independent source-based protocol.
preregistration.promotion_rule: M for exact observed source-directory outcomes, not broader Prolog semantic compatibility or performance; independent SWI only witnesses likes semantics.

result.observed: Original complete 2026-11-18 runner: 4/4 preserved sources; Gen24 Rust original acceptance 0/4, Gen25 1/4 (likes.pl only), other 3 Rust syntax-rejected. SWI 9.0.4 process exit0 on all, but 3 stderr contain ERROR diagnostics, only likes is clean. 12/12 live independent SWI original-source likes answers and 264/264 historical Rust outputs passed. Corrected outcome label must be replayed on final head.
result.effect_size: Typed four-row original-source acceptance shift 0/4 to 1/4; SWI 1 clean load and 3 process-exit0-with-ERROR; 12/12 likes semantic matches; 264/264 Rust regression cases.
result.uncertainty: Single selected upstream public-domain demo directory, some files intentionally invalid or newer syntax than distro SWI 9.0.4; project-authored harness and interpretation; not independent authored empirical study or general language coverage.
retired_claims: SWI exit code 0 always means clean successful source load
Claiming colours.pl intended non-executable note was in README (it is in original source)
Treating this fixed four-file census as universal ISO Prolog acceptance percentage
active_remainder: Independent SWI load diagnostics on newer-source files are version-sensitive
Unmodified external programs with broader supported syntax
Feature-prioritization needs separate source-backed protocol, not inferred from first rejected token
